description: "Echoes of Landing tells the story of the machines NASA has left across the solar system, on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Our scrolling story takes school-age space fans to each piece of hardware, what it did, where it is now and the science it made possible. Each section ends with a fact you can check on NASA's own site, so young readers learn real space history they can trust.
summary:
We built Echoes of Landing, a scroll-driven story about the things humans have left on the Moon and Mars. Instead of a list of missions, it follows the objects themselves: the mirror Apollo 11 left that still reflects lasers from Earth, the rovers parked where their crews left them, a family photo lying in the lunar dust, and Opportunity, which was built for 90 days and kept driving for nearly 15 years.

You start by flying into Buzz Aldrin’s visor, then travel through space to each world. Every object opens from a turning ring of real NASA photographs, with a single short line and a small animation instead of paragraphs. We also included the animals sent before any human, because that is part of the story too.

Most people think of space history as launches and astronauts. We wanted to show what stays behind: quiet evidence of who we were when we got there. These objects will outlast almost everything we build on Earth, and we think that’s worth remembering.
details:
How we built it

We came up with the concept and story, and directed the design through many rounds of feedback on what each scene shows, how it moves, what it says, and what to cut. The website is built with React and Vite, using Framer Motion for animation and Lenis for smooth scrolling. The starfield is drawn on Canvas, and the small story animations are SVG.

The music is generated live in the browser with the Web Audio API, alongside real NASA recordings: Neil Armstrong’s first words on the Moon, and wind on Mars captured by Perseverance’s microphone. Every image is a real mission photo from NASA, JPL, Roscosmos, CNSA or ESA, prepared with Python and FFmpeg. The site is hosted on Vercel.
